requirement:
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.test-coverage.check`. I did not read implementation source or the helpers (`model_tripwire`, `saved_check`, `full_flow`). Each obligation below is judged from the supplied test text. I did not search for further tests beyond the reference listing.

**Obligations derived from the text**
1. `habeas coverage-check` checks saved coverage against the threshold and function rules, and exits successfully only when every obligation is met or excepted.
2. The command does not build the project.
3. The command does not execute tests.
4. The command does not collect coverage.
5. The command does not invoke an assessment model.
6. The detailed rules in the cited `.threshold`, `.functions` and `.exceptions` requirements are context. They belong to those requirements' own tests.

**Mapping to tests**
- **Success path.** `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]` runs the full flow on a passing fixture. It then runs the standalone `saved_check` and asserts success and "Coverage check passed". The standalone check therefore succeeds on saved data when every obligation is met.
- **Failure path for functions.**
  - The same test rewrites the source so the nested `fn hidden` has no execution. The overlapping parent `outer` is executed.
  - It asserts that the flow fails and that stdout contains `#fn[outer]/fn[hidden]: zero execution`. It also asserts that stdout does not contain `#fn[outer]: zero execution`.
  - The standalone `saved_check` then fails with "Coverage check failed". This exercises `check.functions`, including that nested-function execution does not cover the parent.
  - It also asserts that the recorded run outcome stays "success", so the policy caused the failure rather than the tests.
- **Failure path for unmeasured functions.**
  - `fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` captures coverage for a single filtered test.
  - It then runs `habeas coverage-check` directly and asserts a non-zero exit and a "File execution coverage" report.
- **No build, test or collection.**
  - The second test puts a stub `cargo` on `PATH`. The stub records every call and exits 99 for any subcommand other than `metadata`.
  - It asserts the forbidden-command file is absent. It asserts the test-execution sentinel file is absent. It asserts the retained coverage files are byte-identical before and after.
  - The first test also asserts that the `evidence` directory is unchanged after the check.
- **No model.** The first test starts a model tripwire server. It asserts the request count is 0 after both the full flow and the standalone checks.

**Delegated obligations**
- The unit tests in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs` carry `{test}` references to `.threshold`, `.functions`, `.exceptions`, `.report` and `.measurement`. They cover:
  - the exact per-file threshold;
  - accepted, stale and missing exceptions, and the rule that function exceptions do not transfer to other items or the file;
  - unmeasured files;
  - overlapping nested functions;
  - the union of counts across runs.
- These sub-requirements are cited here, not refined through `{impl}`. I did not reassess them. The subject's own tests show the command applying these checks end to end, with success and failure outcomes.
- The accepted-exception success path through the CLI has no end-to-end test here. It is covered at the report level by the `check.exceptions` tests, so I did not count it as a gap.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} check
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
:::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
